items.title: Hands On: HoYoverse's Pokémon Rival Won Me Over - I Just Need It on PS5
items.content:
I’ve never played an auto chess game – or auto battler, as I think the parlance has settled upon.

Despite this, I’m fairly familiar with the format of games like Teamfight Tactics , because it’s a genre one of my favourite developers HoYoverse seems utterly obsessed with.

If you play Honkai: Star Rail with any regularity, you’ll be familiar with the endgame mode Currency Wars, which takes elements from auto battlers and repurposes them for its turn-based combat system.

Similarly, there have been various events in both Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero which have been inspired by auto battlers, including one featuring the cutesy Bangboo characters from the latter release.

I’m not sure whether the giant Chinese dev has been using these activities to gather feedback for Honkai: Nexus Anima , but it’s sure helped me feel comfortable with a genre I’ve never interacted with before.

As part of its intent to corner every part of the gaming market, this new effort from the ever-expanding studio blends the aforementioned Teamfight Tactics-inspired strategy gameplay with Pokémon -esque creature catching.

Having played the game’s recent closed beta for a few hours, I think it’s a compelling blend.

I’m tired of HoYoverse’s nauseous overemphasis on proper nouns, so the narrative here has done little for me, even if there’s clearly plenty of intrigue baked into the game’s cutesy premise.

You’ll already be familiar with some of the characters, like Blade from Honkai: Star Rail and Otto from Honkai Impact 3rd , so it’s quite cool to see the universes converge. But if I see one more subtitle with smallprint explainers positioned within it, I might just explode.

The world itself is vibrant, although it’s not overly dissimilar to the busy blend of urban assets you may already be familiar with in Honkai: Star Rail’s Planarcadia – the latest planet Trailblazers are exploring.

I think what sets this sandbox apart is its emphasis on creatures, which you can obviously capture a la Pokémon and add to your team.

The world feels a lot more alive and interactive than Game Freak’s efforts, even though I don’t think the creature or character designs are quite up to the same standard yet. Of course, that’s an impossibly high bar for Honkai: Nexus Anima to clear.

I do like the tactical auto battler gameplay, although I must concede I don’t really feel like I’ve extracted all of its depth just yet.

In simple terms, for the purposes of this article, different creatures can be placed on the stage fulfilling unique roles. For example, you might use strong, tank-like monsters on the frontline to withstand damage, while backline critters buff or heal.

items.title: REVIEW: The UGreen and Honkai: Star Rail collaboration is both beautiful and powerful
items.summary: As someone who grew up as a fan of Japanese animation, I would often sketch characters that I created in the same style. So, I was looking forward to trying out...
items.content:
As someone who grew up as a fan of Japanese animation, I would often sketch characters that I created in the same style. So, I was looking forward to trying out the UGreen and Honkai Star Rail collaboration. Granted, I don’t play the game, but it’s not hard to be a fan of the character style and animation. All the characters are just gorgeous.

And I was not disappointed upon receiving the box; I was surprised. It was huge, unlike the many PR boxes that I receive; this one was sturdy and well-made. They did not cheap out on the packaging materials.

Honestly, we were not prepared for the unboxing video because of how big the box was, especially when you opened it. If you’re a fan and you are looking for that premium unboxing experience, this collaboration delivers. There’s even a peacock-like plumage that opens like a fan when you open the box. So make sure that you have your camera set up for that unboxing video.

The MagFlow Air Magnetic Power Bank is a beautiful teal blue, which makes it easy to spot in the bag. It is also thin and light, which is always a plus for me. I appreciate that there is a dedicated cord that you can neatly tuck away in the power bank itself. So you don’t lose the cord, and it doesn’t get tangled with other things in your bag. The wireless charging was also impressive. A full charge on the power bank can give two phones a boost.

The Nexode Air 65W Charger and retractable USB-C cable had beautiful designs, but still delivered fast charging. In fact, it is already the dedicated charging setup for my bedside table; I’ve been charging more items with the Nexode setup. It’s a plus that the retractable cable helps keep things organized.

Last but not least, the Fine Track Mini 2, which is also a beautiful teal blue, and I love this, by the way, since it’s a refreshing colorway from the usual black or white of AirTags. This only works with Apple’s Find My network, by the way. The speaker was loud enough to hear, even when it was in another part of the house.

items.title: Hands on with the Honkai: Star Rail v4.0 experience
items.summary: This HoyoVerse train just keeps on chugging!
items.content:
The last article I wrote for Honkai: Star Rail was going over the details of the upcoming Version 4.0 release . Since then, HoYoverse generously offered up the opportunity to play Version 4.0 and experience Planarcadia early. Having spent about a dozen hours or so playing with the new characters, experiencing the story, and generally taking in the sights and sounds of Planarcadia, I’m prepared to share my thoughts on all of it.

It’s best to start off with the main attraction of Version 4.0: Planarcadia. This new planet is a fictional world come to life and boy does it leave a fantastic first impression. Full of the kind of sights and sounds you’d expect from an Asian city brimming with life. Exploration is a blast with all the alleys and little nooks to find, the platforming segments that can either help you navigate across certain parts of the city or find chests within them. There’s also a new style of puzzles that require you to rotate a 2D plane in a 3D space to “paint” certain parts of it to make them solid and let you platform with those objects. Planarcadia is so full of whimsy and still has some of the overhang of a crime family really enabling a super unique feeling planet compared to what we’ve had with previous locations such as the Xianzhou or Amphoreus.

The two new characters following the path of Elation feel great, even if the Aha Moment is a little overstimulating sometimes. Sparxie and Yao Guang fit on a team together like a glove to demolish all the bosses I’ve thrown them against. I’m eager to see where the new path goes with time, especially since we only have the two characters currently. Even as of the live public server branch, we’re unsure when Elation Trailblazer will make their debut, so keep an eye on that as versions progress beyond 4.0. You’ll need to get a hold of new Elation Light Cones as well since they obviously can’t use the other Paths’ options. Burning skill points to increase the Elation stacks until Aha decides he’s satisfied and steps in for a big attack feels really great and it has me curious what future Elation characters might do when they trigger their own Aha Moments.

Not to mention that for new players, you’ve got the opportunity to really kickstart a team of your choice with a new planet. We’re at a point in the game where there’s so many options for characters you can pick from and build around, and 4.0 introducing Elation means that as a new player, you can jump in and get a headstart on pulling for that archetype. Especially with a new Novaflare round of buffs, there’s even more options than before bringing older characters back into the limelight. The Black Swan and Sparkle buffs are so massive that people running DoT teams or any team using an action advance support such as Bronya or Sunday have another insane option. Sparkle was always good, but her Novaflare enables her to further buff your DPS units to extreme levels. Black Swan’s Novaflare was even more insane and rocketed her back up to the top for damage even as a DoT unit. Combined with the option to pick a free character including units like Sparkle, Kafka (who works great in DoT teams), and more, you really can’t go wrong in Planarcadia and the Version 4.0 patch from what I’ve gotten to experience.

Between the free characters, the great change of pace in the story from the latter half of Amphoreus (if you’ve played it, you know), the new cityscape that is quite honestly my new favorite location in the game, and all the new characters to look forward to, you really should make a return to Star Rail if you’ve been away for a minute and are curious about where we’re at. If you’re new, definitely consider giving it a shot. There’s even a bonus to let you convert trace materials for leveling character skills at a 1 to 1 ratio this time instead of a 2 for 1, so you really can kickstart your Elation team. With characters being important again like Silver Wolf, Blade, and Himeko, as well as new faces like Sparxie, Yao Guang, Ashveil, and Pearl, I think 4.0 is just the start of a real treat of a patch cycle for Honkai: Star Rail.

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.4 "In Ravages Does the Whistle Sound" Arrives on July 15
Giving a game another chance
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it. That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I...
items.content:
Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it.

That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I had to stop playing because of bugs. I also stopped because it was really laggy, but I realized when I started playing again this past December that I had actually originally played on the European server rather than the American one, which was why it was lagging.

Now that I’ve started playing it again for the last four months, I’m wishing I’d never quit.

The game’s story is amazing. With games like HSR where the main character is a self-insert, I tend to fully lean into that role. As such, whenever a major twist happens to a character that the main character has bonded with, I really feel it due to the immersion.

Another thing I like about the story is that HSR keeps you on your toes because it isn’t afraid to kill off playable characters.

I’d played a different game from HoYoverse before HSR, and it wouldn’t dream of killing a playable character, so I went into HSR thinking it’d be the same. That idea went out the window on my second day of playing with the first of many playable character deaths.

Because of that, you end up wanting to make sure you own your favorite characters in case you never see them in the game again. However, since HSR is a gacha game, you’re not guaranteed to get the characters you want when they’re available without spending money.

At least that’s what you’d think, but from my experience, HSR is the easiest gacha game I’ve played when it comes to getting the characters you want without spending money.

I’ve managed to get three characters I’ve wanted along with two of their exclusive items without spending money. That’s because HSR makes it really easy to get the in-game currency for pulling characters. That means if you just want to get a character for the sake of having them, you can.

In fact, I’d say HSR is probably the only gacha game where you don’t have to spend real money. I only spent money on cosmetics, but most cosmetics are free rewards from permanent events.

The only negative thing I have to say about the game is that the newer main quests are fairly long.

The latest finished questline takes 62 hours to complete, and the entire main quest line is currently over 100 hours. Because of that, if you have a busy daily schedule, it could take a while to complete. It is possible to finish in a week, but based on personal experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

The length aside, I would highly recommend this game, especially since it’s free on PC and you don’t even need a gaming one as I play on my laptop. With the three years of content in the game so far, I can’t wait to see where it goes from here.

items.title: "Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.2 "So Laughed the Masses" will arrive on April 22"
items.summary: The Path of Elation awaits when Version 4.2 'So Laughed the Masses' launches on April 22nd.
items.content:
SINGAPORE, April 10, 2026 — Global interactive entertainment brand HoYoverse announced today that Honkai: Star Rail's new Version 4.2, "So Laughed the Masses," will officially launch on April 22. With the rewards of Phantasmoon Games receiving a massive escalation, more eyes across the universe will converge on Planarcadia, and the intensity of the competition will greatly increase. Embrace the new power of the Path of Elation, and march towards final victory alongside Silver Wolf LV.999, who has completed her ascension, and the observer Evanescia! Click to watch the latest trailer: https://youtu.be/NyM_seY0XKg

Click here to obtain the media kit: https://hoyoverse.box.com/s/u3ej6hdz0s88q3x75qkx8kr5f5fy3ewb Meanwhile, to celebrate the upcoming third anniversary of Honkai: Star Rail, the game has meticulously prepared a series of special events and generous rewards, inviting players to join in on the fun. In Version 4.2, the anniversary-exclusive event "Festive Gifts" will make its return, allowing players to check in and receive a total of 20 pulls. Also returning is another highly anticipated player tradition: on the anniversary day of April 26, Trailblazers can select a blessing card from a companion and receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. Not to mention, the third-anniversary birthday surprises are an absolute must-see: the limited 5-star characters Huohuo and Robin will be added to the "Stellar Convergence" Store. As is tradition, Trailblazers can use a freely claimed Golden Companion Spirit to exchange for their companion of choice in the store. Furthermore, in addition to the annual first-time top-up double bonus reset, there's even more content waiting for players to explore, including new arrivals in the Gift of Stardust Store and a new Outfit for Castorice! As the anniversary celebration approaches, participate in the "Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere" online event and leave your message for a chance to win multiple grand prizes, including a "Crown of Aha" Silver Wolf LV.999-themed car. At the same time, global cities such as Tokyo, Seoul, and Los Angeles will progressively launch a series of online and offline celebration activities, including themed parades, street festivities, and brand collaborations. For more details, please visit the official website: https://hoyo.link/GXrf0ZdtR In the Version 4.2 Main Story, the stakes of the Phantasmoon Games become a whole lot more complicated once it's announced that the ultimate reward has received an unprecedented escalation: the victor will become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Caught right in the center of the spotlight, the Trailblazer naturally draws the scrutiny and wariness of every major faction. At that moment, Fulwish — leader of the Research Society of Happy Smiles and a local media mogul — invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV headquarters in Seafeld City, a holiday resort renowned for its crisp scenery and idyllic climate. There, Fulwish plans to host a televised debate open to all of arcadia, exploring the burning question: "What kind of future will the Phantasmoon Games bring to this world?" For the Trailblazer, this "public provocation" is undoubtedly an overt scheme that is impossible to refuse. And beneath the surface of the debate lurks a myriad of traps and tricks. Pitted against Fulwish, a master at swaying minds and inciting public opinion, can the Trailblazer navigate every hurdle, gather more Wishpower, and resolve the hidden crisis? Meanwhile, fellow Supplicants Silver Wolf and Pearl have struck a mysterious deal that might just be the key to turning the tide of battle. With the competition heating up, two brand-new 5-star characters Silver Wolf LV.999 and Evanescia will officially join the team, becoming crucial companions to help the Trailblazer turn the tables. First up, a familiar face: Silver Wolf is making her grand entrance with a brand-new look. As a long-time member of the Stellaron Hunters, she needs no introduction. If you had to pick the universe's most hardcore gamer, Silver Wolf takes the crown, hands down. If you treat the vast universe as a game of endless level ups and progress, then "Silver Wolf LV.999" is what happens when she hits level 999 and evolves into a "Godmode Player." This hacker from Punklorde also happens to be the very first Emanator of the Elation from the Phantasmoon Games to step into the spotlight. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-star Imaginary character following the Path of Elation. In combat, she can rack up "Hidden MMR" to activate her exclusive Cartridge and enter the "Godmode Player" state. Once active, Silver Wolf pulls both teammates and enemies alike into her own gaming domain, unlocking a "Reward stage" at the start of her turn. During this "Reward stage," she can use her Cartridge to spawn various in-game items, not only shaking up the combat dynamics but also sharing powerful buffs with teammates to turn the tide together. When "Aha Instant" strikes, Silver Wolf blasts all enemies with a game-crashing laser cannon, dealing massive DMG. On top of that, this hacker from Punklorde has one more trick up her sleeve: when a teammate falls under enemy control, she'll hack into the battlefield — even if she isn't actively in the team — granting allies temporary immunity to control. It's her own special way of keeping the team protected during every battle. Next up is Evanescia. Since the start of the Phantasmoon Games, this mysterious girl has always been watching this game's progress as an observer. In fact, as a "Special Observer," Evanescia has participated in far more than just one iteration of the Phantasmoon Games. Because of this, this multi-playthrough player has already witnessed way too many contestants scheming against one another to fight for Wishpower, and watched countless people repeatedly clash on the heels of Aeonic power. Rather than looking forward to who will become the ultimate champion of the Phantasmoon Games, she pays much more attention to the performance of her favored "protagonist": the Trailblazer. And in the new story, more secrets regarding Evanescia's true identity will also gradually reach a final revelation. Evanescia is a 5-star Physical character following the Path of Elation. In combat, Evanescia can continuously accumulate "Certified Banger" through various means: whether she regenerates Energy, teammates Charge her, or the "Certified Banger" on her teammates changes, she continues to gain "Certified Banger." Whenever Evanescia gains "Certified Banger," she will simultaneously regenerate Energy, allowing her to maintain her DMG rhythm. As "Certified Banger" continues to accumulate, Evanescia's DMG will also gradually increase. Whenever it reaches a certain number of points, it will additionally trigger an attack from "Master Fox," dealing DMG to all enemies and regenerating Energy for Evanescia. Her Elation Skill can also attack all enemies. While delivering a stylish performance, it will further increase the team's overall DMG. In addition to the two highly anticipated new characters, the Trailblazer on the Path of Elation will also join the team in Version 4.2. As the Elation Trailblazer's brand-new weapon, the glow stick features a rich variety of uses. When using their Skill, the glow stick transforms into a lightblade as the Trailblazer deals DMG to all enemies and gains "Certified Banger". Not only that, the glow stick can also turn into nunchucks, unleashing a spectacular flurry of attacks on surrounding enemies and dealing multiple instances of DMG. Beyond that, it can also be used to hype up teammates. When using their Ultimate, the Trailblazer can select a teammate to cheer for. This allows the chosen teammate to gain "Certified Banger" while immediately using their Elation Skill, paving the way for an even more lively combat experience! Additionally, a special Warp event will kick off in the first half of Version 4.2. Limited 5-star characters The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly will be getting a rerun. Meanwhile, in the Warp event for the second half, limited 5-star characters Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao will also have their reruns. On top of that, four existing characters — Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt — will all be receiving buffs, continuing to provide indispensable help for players on their trailblazing expedition. Finally, right in time for the 3rd Anniversary of Honkai: Star Rail, a host of exciting events will be arriving alongside the grand festivities. In Version 4.2, the brand-new event "Cosmic Data Roaming" will officially go live, allowing Trailblazers to build a top-tier streamer career by broadcasting their sleekest combat moments. Following the version update, Currency Wars will also receive a massive expansion, offering Trailblazers more diverse gameplay options. Meanwhile, the Cosmicon Collective is bringing the heat with its Version 2.0 update, "Cosmicon, Roll On Again!," introducing not only new decks and dice, but also a brand-new team challenge gameplay mode. In addition, exciting events and features like "Express Renovation Escapade" and "Relic Recon" will also be rolling out to help Trailblazers fully enjoy the anniversary fun. At the end of this Special Program, the original animation project co-produced by HoYoverse and MAPPA premiered its concept trailer, "Death in the Afternoon." Please look forward to the continuing cosmic adventures! Honkai: Star Rail is now available on PC, iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and PS5, and has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms. In 2023, the game won Apple's App Store iPhone Game of the Year, Google Play's Best Game, and BEST MOBILE GAME by The Game Awards. In 2024, it received the Golden Joystick Awards Still Playing Award (Mobile) and PlayStation® Partner Awards 2024 PARTNER AWARD among other honors. The game has been rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 12. If you wish to learn more details, please visit https://hsr.hoyoverse.com or follow @HonkaiStarRail on Twitter (X), Instagram, and Facebook. Combined with the intuitive turn-based combat system, diverse and distinctive companions, and immersive storylines that together compose an interstellar melody filled with captivating worlds, each brimming with unique cultures, awe-inspiring landscapes, and mythical wonders to explore. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies, and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. items.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.0 impressions
items.content:
I'll admit, I recently burned out on Honkai: Star Rail. Upon hearing the news that 3.8 would be the lengthiest patch yet and with content more sparse than ever before, I decided to take a break for the first time since I started playing all the way back in 1.0. The entire Amphoreus saga left me feeling drained; I thoroughly enjoyed 3.0-3.4 as excellent set-up chapters, but felt lost as the plot became a labyrinth of hidden motivations, layered twists, hours of exposition, and endless proper nouns. When looking at the story as a whole, I love the characters (Aglaea and Anaxa in particular) and the rich history of the world within the Scepter, but the later patches often felt like studying for a needlessly convoluted test. I understood the gist of what was happening, but I won't lie to you and say I could describe to you in detail what Cyrene's deal is or how Evernight fits into everything.

All that's to say: I was looking forward to the Astral Express crew taking a well-earned vacation to Planarcadia, the planet of Elation. Despite two of the game's four current versions ostensibly beginning with Akivili's disciples deciding that they need a break from the backbreaking work of saving the universe, neither has resulted in our trailblazers seeing much downtime. Unlike previous excursions, it's all hands on deck: everyone gets off at this stop (save for Black Swan's incredibly hasty and unfortunate exit prior to departure). It's fun to see the entire main cast get involved, none more welcome than Himeko — up until now, the only character trait I could've told you about her was that she's terrible at making coffee. Getting some elaboration on her backstory and giving her a personality outside of "Express mom" is long overdue.

The Trailblazer and March 7th begin their Planarcadian getaway with a suitably devious greeting by none other than our old pal Sparkle. We're given a tour of the vibrant, totally-not-Japanese-inspired streets, crawling with humans living in tentative harmony with totally-not-Penaconian-memetic-entities known as imagenae. Here, we catch a glimpse of what I hope will become one of Planarcadia's core themes: gentrification and the plight of capitalism, with a side of anti-imperialism (all perpetrated by the IPC, of course). It's bold, though, and I worry that future patches will keep these criticisms in the background rather than highlight them as Planarcadia's core issues. I would love so much for little nuggets of lore to be elaborated upon, ones that suggest a more serious political history than Aha would have you believe: what did the imagenae do before the IPC forced them to integrate into society? Were they not allowed to work at all? Were they marginalized and seen as second-class citizens? Is the Department of Aberration Defense an inherently evil organization left to determine on their own which imagenae deserve their continued existence and which do not? Is Kuchiba so hot that it doesn't even matter?

This brings us to the Synwish Syndicate, a gang formerly designed to be a respite for imagenae that feel rejected elsewhere, now, due to IPC intervention, a gang that largely exists to enable monetary gain by questionable means. Here at the syndicate's headquarters, the plot quickly begins to balloon into what feels like a collection of introductions for what's to come. We have Pearl's cold and calculating grip on the planet, Himeko and her confounding family history, the potential return of the Herald of Death, the Stellaron Hunters' unknown involvement in the Phantasmoon Games, Sunday's inadvertent entry into the Games, Evanescia's whole...thing, and Yao Guang's bottomless supply of divinations. What's most shocking is that the patch still manages to pull off a fun (if bloated) self-contained story, adding layers to one of HSR's most inscrutable characters and ending things with one of the game's best low-stakes twists.

I'm no Xianzhou Arbiter-General, but I can pretty easily peer into the future and divine a prophecy for Honkai: Star Rail: each new patch will introduce and/or discuss at length a new prophecy that cryptically divulges the fate of a character and/or planet and/or simulation masquerading as a planet. It's hard to pinpoint the moment a theme becomes a crutch, but I think HSR passed that moment long ago. In this patch, we have not one, not two, but three central characters that are defined by their relationship with prophecy and prediction — Yao Guang, Pearl, and the perennial mystery that is Elio and his script. So many in-game conversations devolve into the interpretation of prophecy, and frankly, it's becoming exhausting. We went through an entire version in which each Chrysos Heir had a poetically vague predetermined fate, and before that (and in 3.8's ret-con-y confusion) we had Sparkle's ambiguous "three deaths" for Firefly.

If this were a wholesale replacement for well-executed foreshadowing, we would have a far bigger issue. It's obvious, though, that the writing team knows how to tell a story sans-prophecy, evident in Sparkle's character-driven narrative in this very patch. Sparxie being the "true" Sparkle (as much as old Sparkle is also the "true" Sparkle) is teased so perfectly; the reveal is obvious in retrospect while being difficult to predict with the given information. It's consistently groan-inducing to see this writing cheat code being used ad nauseam within a story that could function better without it. I hope I'll be proven wrong and the game will subvert the words of its murky prophets, leaving me with egg on my face come the conclusion of this leg of the Express' journey.

4.0 is a promising new beginning, and has at the very least brought me back in terms of its story. Though there is an abundance of new proper nouns to memorize and a bevy of new and returning cast members to keep track of, the patch still takes on a welcome return to simplicity and levity (save for the shocking tonal shift right at the end, RIP the Synwish Syndicate Feb. 2026 - Feb. 2026). As long as things don't get too bogged down in extensive metaphors and tiresome exposition, I'm hopeful that Planarcadia can become the most focused version of HSR we've seen so far.
